title: Non-blocking follow-ups from backend-trade-strategy-tagging review (PR #218)
description: Non-blocking findings from the pr-reviewer pass on PR #218 (free-text strategy tag on positions/closed trades), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's convention so they aren't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: PositionIn.strategy has no field_validator to strip whitespace or normalize an empty string to null (mirrors the already-tracked entry_notes gap in backend-trade-journal-entry-notes-followups). Concretely: an explicit `strategy: ""` on a merge is falsy under `if position.strategy:` so it correctly leaves the existing tag untouched, but a whitespace-only value like `"   "` is truthy and would silently overwrite an existing tag with whitespace -- untested today. Decide whether strategy should strip/normalize the same way ticker does (or the entry_notes decision, once made, should apply here too), and record the decision.

No case/whitespace normalization is enforced on `strategy`, so two otherwise-identical tags that differ only in casing or incidental whitespace (e.g. "Pullback to value" vs "pullback to value ") would land in separate exact-match buckets. This directly undermines the stated purpose of overwrite-on-merge (a single clean value for exact-match grouping) once the future backend-trade-apgar task and the ch. 59 equity-curves-segmented-by-strategy idea actually start grouping by this field. Worth reconsidering (e.g. trim + case-fold on write, or a suggest-from-existing-values UX in the eventual frontend) before those consumers land, though out of scope for this task.

decisions.decision: Added `PositionIn._strip_and_normalize_strategy`, a field_validator on `strategy` that strips leading/trailing whitespace and normalizes a resulting empty string to `None` -- exactly mirroring `PositionIn._strip_and_normalize_entry_notes` (backend-trade-journal-entry-notes-followups). This also fixes the merge-overwrite bug for free: `add_position`'s `if position.strategy:` check now correctly treats a whitespace-only incoming tag as falsy (it's already `None` by the time the handler runs), so it no longer silently overwrites an existing tag with whitespace.
decisions.rationale: The checklist item itself points at applying 'the entry_notes decision, once made' here too, and that decision (backend-trade-journal-entry-notes-followups) already established the reasoning for this exact shape on a structurally identical field: `strategy` is optional free-text just like `entry_notes`, so an explicit blank/whitespace-only value has no meaningful difference from omitting the field entirely -- silently normalizing to `None` (matching the already-omitted case) is more useful than a 422 that would force the caller to strip client-side, and avoids leaking an inconsistent `""` vs `null` distinction through the API the way `ticker`'s stricter reject-on-blank approach would if applied here (ticker is required and non-optional, unlike `strategy`). Considered leaving `strategy` exempt from normalization on the theory that it's a newer, less-tested field than `entry_notes` -- rejected because the underlying whitespace-truthiness bug is identical in both cases (both gate a merge-time `if`), and PR #218's own review flagged it as directly analogous to the already-fixed `entry_notes` gap, so there was no reason to reach a different answer here.

decisions.decision: `strategy` is NOT case-folded (or otherwise casing-normalized) on write. Casing is preserved exactly as the caller typed it, after the whitespace-strip normalization above. No trim+case-fold-on-write or suggest-from-existing-values UX was implemented in this task.
decisions.rationale: Considered case-folding on write (e.g. lowercasing, or title-casing) so that 'Pullback to value' and 'pullback to value' land in the same exact-match bucket for a future strategy-segmented consumer -- rejected for two reasons. First, `strategy` is not a purely internal grouping key: `PositionOut.strategy`/`ClosedTradeOut.strategy` echo the exact same value straight back to the trader as their own display label (there is no separate display-vs-storage representation anywhere in this schema), so silently rewriting a trader's own deliberate casing (e.g. 'IPO lockup expiry' vs a case-folded 'ipo lockup expiry') would be a surprising, irreversible loss of their own input with no way to recover the original -- a materially different tradeoff than the whitespace-strip decision above, which discards nothing a reasonable caller would have intentionally relied on. Second, checking the actual current consumer confirms there is no live grouping need yet to force the tradeoff now: `backend-trade-apgar` (the concrete consumer named in this checklist item) shipped as a single fixed 5-question set scored identically for every ticker regardless of `strategy`'s value (see its own `decisions` entry) -- it does not group or bucket by `strategy` at all -- and the ch. 59 'equity curves segmented by strategy' idea remains an unimplemented `docs/ideas.md` entry, not a task on the board. Implementing case-folding speculatively, before any real consumer's exact grouping semantics are known (case-insensitive comparison at read time vs. case-folding at write time are both still live options depending on what that consumer actually needs), risks solving the wrong problem. Deferring matches the checklist item's own framing ('worth reconsidering... before those consumers land') and its own suggested alternative (a suggest-from-existing-values autocomplete UX in a future frontend task) is preferable precisely because it also preserves the trader's original casing for display while still nudging them toward reusing an existing tag -- something a write-time case-fold cannot do. When a future consumer does need case-insensitive exact-match grouping, it should compare case-insensitively (e.g. `.strip().casefold()`) at query/aggregation time rather than mutating the stored value, so the trader's own display text is never silently rewritten.

comments.summary: Blocking: the new description text is factually wrong about `entry_notes`. `PositionIn.strategy`'s Field description, `add_position`'s docstring (backend/app/api/routers/portfolio.py), backend/openapi.json, and frontend/src/api/types.ts all now say 'unlike `entry_notes` -- its casing is preserved as typed rather than case-folded', implying `entry_notes` IS case-folded on write. It is not: `_strip_and_normalize_entry_notes` only strips whitespace and normalizes blank-to-null, exactly like the new `_strip_and_normalize_strategy` -- verified directly by instantiating `PositionIn(entry_notes='Pullback To Value')`, which returns 'Pullback To Value' unchanged (no case-folding at all). The real, and only, asymmetry between the two fields is merge semantics (strategy overwrites, entry_notes appends), not case handling. This false claim is now committed into the OpenAPI contract in 4 places, which CLAUDE.md's API documentation standard requires be accurate ('well-explained, not just correctly typed') -- a future reader could reasonably build a dedup/display feature assuming entry_notes values differing only in case are already merged into one canonical casing, which they are not. Needs a reword (e.g. 'unlike `entry_notes`, which is merged by appending rather than overwriting, and is likewise never case-folded') in all 4 locations plus a re-export of openapi.json/types.ts.

Non-blocking: `PositionIn._strip_and_normalize_entry_notes` and the new `_strip_and_normalize_strategy` now have byte-for-byte identical bodies (strip; normalize empty string to None). `field_validator` accepts multiple field names in one call (`@field_validator("entry_notes", "strategy")`), so these could be consolidated into one validator to avoid the duplication. Tracked as a followup checklist item on backend-trade-strategy-tagging-followups-followups; no correctness impact.

review.notes: Full review performed. Backend suite: `pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing` -- 1144 passed, 99.89% coverage (gate 90%), no regression. Static analysis clean: ruff, mypy, `yarn lint`, `yarn tsc -b --noEmit`, scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py, scripts/validate_tasks.py all pass with zero findings. Confirmed the regression test genuinely reproduces the fixed bug: temporarily removed `_strip_and_normalize_strategy` and re-ran test_merge_with_whitespace_only_incoming_strategy_leaves_existing_strategy_unchanged -- it failed with `'   ' == 'Pullback to value'` as expected, then restored the validator (checked out the file back to HEAD) and reconfirmed the full suite passes; the whitespace-merge-overwrite bug fix itself is real, not just documented. Independently verified the backend-trade-apgar claim by reading backend/app/portfolio/trade_apgar.py directly: it implements Elder's ch. 58 fixed 5-question set scored identically per ticker with no reference to `strategy` anywhere in the module or its router usage -- the decisions entry's claim that it doesn't group by strategy is accurate. Regenerated backend/openapi.json myself via `python scripts/export_openapi.py` and diffed against the committed snapshot: zero diff, confirming it's current and in sync (no stale-snapshot issue) -- but see the blocking comment above: 'in sync' does not mean 'accurate', and the newly-added description text itself contains a factual error about entry_notes' behavior, caught by re-reading the diff and independently testing PositionIn(entry_notes=...) directly. Both decisions entries (whitespace-normalize; do-not-case-fold) are themselves sound, each with rejected alternatives and rationale, and both trace back to a checklist item asking for exactly that judgment call -- no undecided-but-implemented gap; the blocking issue is in how the code's own comments/description describe an unrelated existing field, not in the decisions or the actual `strategy` behavior. area is backend/portfolio, so verify-elder-signal was run: this change touches only the strategy free-text tag (a journaling field per Analyse.md's ch. 55/56/58/59 references), not Screen 1/2/3, the Impulse gate, confidence scoring, or the portfolio risk overlay -- none of that checklist applies. architecture-review not run: no new module/dependency/layer added. No frontend components touched (types.ts is the generated API client only) and no backend endpoint behavior visible to a user changed in a way that needed exercising through a UI -- explicitly no UI surface, so the browser walkthrough (step 9) and persisted e2e suite (step 9a) were both skipped on that basis rather than silently omitted. Also ran the code-review skill (background), which independently surfaced the same two findings (the entry_notes casing inaccuracy, and the validator duplication) -- corroborating both. One non-blocking reuse/simplification finding filed as a followup task (backend-trade-strategy-tagging-followups-followups); the blocking finding goes back to the task-worker via this needs_work verdict instead. Note: mid-review, an errant `git stash pop` (called without first checking `git stash list`) transiently applied a pre-existing, unrelated stash from a prior incident (dated 2026-09-18, explicitly labeled 'not mine, do not discard') onto this working tree, producing conflicts in Makefile/docs/tasks files unrelated to this PR. Resolved immediately via `git reset --hard HEAD` before any commit was made; the pre-existing stash entries are confirmed still intact and untouched in `git stash list` (stash@{0}, stash@{1}), and this PR's branch was not affected. Flagging for visibility per the shared-working-tree caution in CLAUDE.md, even though no lasting effect occurred.
